heroHeadline: GSF Day 1 Full Operations; MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 24 Closed; 1,100+ Newly Displaced from Artibonite
heroSubtitle: June 2, 2026 marks the first full operational day of the UN-authorized Gang Suppression Force (GSF) following its formal June 1 launch. The advance force of approximately 800 personnel (Chad ~400, Guatemala ~75, El Salvador ~70) — roughly 15% of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling under UNSCR 2793 — remains exclusively deployed in Port-au-Prince's city center corridor under Mongolian Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri's command. Cité Soleil, Martissant, the Artibonite, Centre, and Sud-Est have zero GSF coverage. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital — the only health facility accessible to approximately 300,000 commune residents — enters its 24th consecutive day of forced closure and its longest uninterrupted shutdown since the 2021 crisis began. IOM's Emergency Tracking Tool Report 95 (covering May 29–June 1) documents over 1,100 newly displaced persons from Petite Rivière de Bayonnais (Artibonite) who fled to Gonaïves following gang violence on May 26; UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric confirmed ongoing Artibonite displacement on June 1. National IDP total remains at approximately 1.5 million confirmed by the UN on May 29, with 600,000+ in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe/near-famine) conditions. The 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains approximately 23% funded ($198.7M of $880M). The US Supreme Court ruling on TPS for approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals is expected in late June–early July 2026.
